proven_unit.proposition: For all primes p>3, original signed 2304 grade-2 V2,p = Σ_{n=(p+1)/2}^{floor((3p-1)/4)}(8n+1)C_n ≡0 mod p^3; hence P_N(1)=0 in F_p for N=floor((p-3)/4), where P_N is the exact earlier original-grade-2 polynomial.
proven_unit.proof_basis: Guo--Zudilin 2019 Theorem 1.1: same original 2304 full and half truncations both ≡ p(-3/p) mod p^3. Their difference =V2+V3, with each term of V3 divisible p^3 by v_p(C_n)=floor(4n/p). Earlier Kp-unit polynomial identity then implies P_N(1)=0.
proven_unit.source: Victor J. W. Guo; Wadim Zudilin, A q-microscope for supercongruences, Advances in Mathematics 346 (2019) 329-358, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2019.02.008, https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.01830, Theorem 1.1 and equations (2)(3).

second_unit.theorem: Q2=V2/p^3, Q3=V3/p^3, D=(Vfull-Vhalf)/p^3 all defined in Fp and D=Q2+Q3 modulo p.

second_unit.conclusion: V2 is uniformly p^3-divisible, but its fourth-digit Q2 can be nonzero. Retain -2Q2 in AF4 signed fourth-digit interface.
